title: Output of the majority loop
statement: Let $V$ be a language of bit strings, let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers, and let $z$ be a bit string. Put $N=a'(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^{k'}$, and for each $j<N$ let $B_j$ be the length-$a(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^k$ block of $\pi_2(z)$ beginning at position $j a(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^k$. Iterating the prescribed block-loop step from its prescribed initialization and concatenating the emissions for $N+1$ iterations yields the one-bit list whose bit is true exactly when $N<2\,|\{j<N: \langle\pi_1(z),B_j\rangle\in V\}|$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of bit strings
